title: The Artinian Lex-Plus-Powers Betti Theorem
main_claim: Over C, for any homogeneous I containing a regular sequence of degrees 2<=a_1<=...<=a_n in n variables, the lex-plus-powers ideal J exists, is an ideal with the same Hilbert function, and beta_{p,j}(S/I) <= beta_{p,j}(S/J) for all p,j (Artinian EGH + LPP). The corollary extends this to any char-0 field and any length c, using the Caviglia–Maclagan and Caviglia–Kummini reductions.
coverage: I read all sections (1–8) in full and checked each step. Sec. 1 (forms): the cited Theorem 1.1 of the companion paper matches the companion's actual statement, including the left-Delta t-basis of the full algebra Delta[x]. There is no circularity: the companion cites this paper only for the interface. Sec. 2: the leading-submodule comparison checks out (filtration placing position alpha at alpha+1_sigma, gr complex = K(E/in W), rank d >= rank gr d). Sec. 3: checked the resolution transfer. Minimality holds because the right T-basis b_u sits in degree 0 and f b_u expands to degree-e polynomials in t; flatness holds since N = Delta⊗_C S. V_alpha is a left ideal, so it is 0 or Delta. P ⊆ M follows from the reverse-index lex order putting a_h e_h first. Sec. 4: checked the distraction D, the commutation identity, D(P)=P (uses a_h<=a_ℓ), the intertwining maps C_v, the prefix-count monotonicity and strictness (coefficient -(1-zeta^{u_ℓ})/(1-zeta) ≠ 0), and termination. Sec. 5: checked that p(v) preserves order, the zero-slice tail-filling inequality, the top slice by reflected complement, and the shadow count |∂X| = |∂'X(0)| + |X| - |X(b_r)|. Sec. 6: checked the reduction mod z, the slice decomposition, annihilation of the middle slices via box stability, that the Koszul deficit is monotone under submodules and quotients, and the endpoint containments G^(0) ⊆ Λ'H^(0) and Λ'H^(a-1) ⊆ G^(a-1). Sec. 7: box-lex + P equals the full lex segment + P. Sec. 8: checked the field descent. I did not verify the external reductions CM08 Prop. 10 and CK14 Thm. 4.1 against the original papers.

issues.location: Sec. 8, proof of Corollary 1.2 (char-0, arbitrary length c)
issues.description: The non-Artinian extension rests on CM08 Prop. 10 and CK14 Thm. 4.1, but their exact hypotheses are not restated. For example, CK14 may need the Artinian LPP for an extended sequence such as (f_1..f_c, x_{c+1}^N, ...) rather than for the images f̄_i in C[x_1..x_c]. Theorem 1.1 covers any full-length sequence with degrees >=2, so it should apply in either form. Still, the paper does not show that the cited reduction is applied with matching hypotheses.
issues.evidence: 'The Artinian reduction of Caviglia--Maclagan [Prop 10] transfers the Hilbert-function assertion... Theorem 4.1 of Caviglia--Kummini transfers the Betti assertion as well.' The exact form of the Artinian input those results require is not quoted.

sibling_notes: Companion paper (rank 322, Commuting-Division-Coefficient-Forms...) was reported no_gap_found. This paper depends entirely on that paper's Thm 1.1 for the reduction step. Everything after the reduction re-proves the Mermin–Murai monomial LPP and checks out.
